title: Work-Authorization Continuity Benefit for Care Employers
one_liner: An employer-paid benefit that screens every care worker for legal pathways, tracks EAD renewals and reverification, and plans backfill.
customer: Home-care agencies, nursing homes and assisted-living groups with 50-2,000 workers, especially in NY, FL, MA, MN, WI and CA, and staffing agencies.
problem: 30% of direct care workers are immigrants (60% in New York), and about 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4. At least one in five immigrant direct-care workers come from countries hit by the 75-country visa pause. With turnover already at 77-80%, losing staff means closed beds, and few workers have been screened for family, asylum, adjustment or other pathways.
solution: A per-worker monthly benefit: confidential attorney-led status screening and pathway triage, EAD and renewal tracking with on-time filing, an I-9 reverification calendar with non-discriminatory templates, workforce-at-risk forecasting by site and date, and fast backfill through a partner training school. Employers see aggregate risk, not individual status.
why_now: The 2026 visa pause, TPS terminations and a DOL proposal to roll back home-care wage protections hit at once, and Wisconsin agencies say they're 'just not able to take new clients.' Employers need something other than lobbying.
revenue_model: $8-15 per worker per month (employer-paid), plus filing fees with 20-30% margin and optional filing-fee financing.
non_obvious_insight: Immigration compliance is treated as static HR paperwork, but for care employers it is now a retention and continuity problem. Attorney-led screening can surface pathways that keep workers, which is worth thousands per retained caregiver.
first_30_days: Partner with an immigration law firm and a Haitian community organization, sign three agencies with Haitian-heavy workforces (NY, FL, MA), and pilot with 200 workers.

title: Roll-Up of Compounding-Stranded Weight-Loss Clinics
one_liner: Buy distressed med spas and weight-loss clinics that lost their compounded GLP-1 margin, and convert them into aftercare-plus-aesthetics businesses.
customer: The clinics' patients, who pay memberships and procedures. Sellers are owners of weight-loss clinics, med spas and telehealth shells.
problem: FDA proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list on Apr 30, 2026 and sent ~55 warning letters to telehealth firms in Mar and Jun. Reportedly ~60% of med spas offered GLP-1 programs by 2025, many on compounded supply that peaked at ~30% of US volume. Owners want out, yet PE physician-practice deals are down ~50% in 2026, so buyers are scarce.
solution: Acquire 10-20 clinics at 0.3-0.8x revenue with seller notes and earn-outs. Convert to branded pill and vial cash programs, plus aftercare (muscle, nutrition, dose step-down), legal peptide offerings and aesthetics upsells. Centralize the medical director, billing and marketing.
why_now: The compounding cliff has stranded assets that are just patient relationships and licenses, while buyer capital retreated. 63% of 'Ozempic face' patients are cosmetic-clinic first-timers, so aesthetics cross-sell is real.
revenue_model: Clinic revenue of $199-399/month memberships plus procedures. Target ~25% EBITDA after integration, with a shared-services center.
non_obvious_insight: Distress plus absent buyers means near-free customer bases, and revenue per patient can rise after the switch to branded drugs plus aftercare. Earn-outs limit downside if patients churn.
first_30_days: Pull state med-spa and pharmacy lists and Instagram GLP-1 advertisers. Contact 100 owners, sign 2 LOIs with seller notes, and close the first acquisition of $150-300k with an integration playbook.

title: Fry-Oil Co-op Escaping Evergreen Renderer Contracts
one_liner: Aggregate independent restaurants' used cooking oil, sell it to biofuel buyers at market with sensor-verified traceability, and hand the owner the check the big renderer keeps.
customer: Independent restaurants and small chains with 2-20 fryer-heavy units are the supply side and pay no fee. Local independent oil collectors, biodiesel, renewable diesel and SAF feedstock processors and brokers are the demand side and pay the co-op. Revenue is the spread plus a small sensor rental fee.
problem: Used fry oil is a commodity that biofuel makers have been bidding up, yet independents are locked into 3-year auto-renewing pickup contracts with a large renderer or bin company. The restaurant is paid a pittance or nothing, or is even charged fees. Bins overflow, which brings health-code and odor problems. Thieves steal oil at night, and nobody reconciles what the oil is actually worth. Owners don't switch because the termination window is a 60-90 day certified-letter deadline buried in the contract, and nobody has time to run a bid.
solution: A co-op platform that: (1) tracks each member's contract renewal date and files the non-renewal notice on time; (2) runs a monthly reverse auction among local collectors so that volume, not the restaurant, gets the price; (3) installs a roughly $40 ultrasonic fill sensor and a lockable tank cap, so pickups trigger at 80% full and every pickup is photo- or QR-verified; (4) issues a statement per pickup indexed to a published used-cooking-oil price series; and (5) produces per-restaurant chain-of-custody records that renewable-fuel producers need to prove domestic, traceable feedstock.
why_now: As I understand it, federal clean-fuel incentives (45Z) now favor North American feedstock, and concern about mislabeled imported used oil has raised the value of traceable domestic oil. Renewable diesel and SAF capacity keeps growing. Cheap cellular fill sensors are widely available. Restaurants' margins are so thin that any found cash gets attention. Verify the current feedstock price index and the 45Z sourcing rules before you pitch.
revenue_model: 20-30% spread on oil sold, indexed and transparent, plus $10-30 per month for the sensor and tank lock. Later add a premium for verified-traceable oil sold to fuel producers, and carbon-intensity documentation fees.
non_obvious_insight: The incumbent's real product is the locked contract and route density, not the oil service, so the way in is the calendar rather than a better price. The contract renewal date is the CRM key: a 90-day-out certified non-renewal letter, filed for the owner, is the growth engine. Owners think they are getting 'free removal', so nobody shops it. Also, per-restaurant traceability is worth more to fuel buyers than the oil's volume alone.
first_30_days: Walk one restaurant row and photograph each bin's contract label, and note the pickup company and renewal date for 40 restaurants in one metro. Sign one local collector or small biodiesel maker as a buyer with a written price index. Enroll 8-10 off-contract or month-to-month members, including my own two locations. Install sensors and lock caps, run the first monthly auction, and show each owner a side-by-side statement of what their old vendor paid versus what the co-op did.

title: Child-in-the-Room Detector for Voice AI
one_liner: A tiny on-device SDK that infers from a few seconds of speech whether a speaker is likely a child, so voice assistants, cars, TVs and toys can drop into a safe policy tier without any login, camera or ID.
customer: OEMs of smart speakers, TVs and in-car assistants, voice-AI and companion app makers, and toy makers.
problem: Ambient voice AI serves shared households with no account or age signal. Laws and probes (CA SB 243, the FTC 6(b) inquiry, COPPA 'actual knowledge') create duties once a minor is present. Devices cannot tell a child from an adult, and asking kids to log in fails. The amended COPPA rule's biometric coverage makes storing voiceprints risky.
solution: An SDK under 5MB that classifies speaker age band (under 9, 9-15, adult) with calibrated confidence and an abstain option, using ephemeral features and never storing voiceprints. It returns a 'minor-likely' signal to trigger safe modes (topic limits, no romance roleplay, safe-messaging protocols) with audit logs. It is benchmarked publicly across accents and speech differences and fails safe by default.
why_now: Lawsuits and the FTC inquiry are pushing platforms to prove they detect minors, on-device speech encoders are good enough, and the brief flags a demand for privacy-preserving, non-ID age signals.
revenue_model: Per-device royalty of $0.10-0.50 or per-MAU pricing, plus paid integration and benchmark-certification services.
non_obvious_insight: For a voice product, the best age signal is the voice itself, with no ID, camera or login. The error costs are asymmetric: treating an adult as a child is cheap, the reverse is not, so 'fail safe' is the sales pitch.
first_30_days: Fine-tune an open speech encoder on licensed or consented child and adult speech corpora. Publish an open benchmark and baseline. Talk to 10 voice-AI and toy builders. Land 2 paid pilots at $3-5k each.

title: Statutory Records-Portal Autopilot for Florida HOAs
one_liner: An email-in service that auto-posts a small Florida condo or HOA board's required documents to a compliant owner-only portal and tracks the deadlines.
customer: Self-managed Florida condo associations with 25+ units and HOAs with 100+ parcels, run by volunteer boards who cannot afford enterprise community-management software. The board treasurer or secretary pays, on the advice of the association's attorney or CPA.
problem: Florida law now requires these associations to post official records online. Condos of 25+ units must post the declaration and bylaws, minutes and meeting videos for the preceding 12 months, contracts and bid summaries over $500, budgets, financial reports, meeting notices and inspection reports and reserve studies, within 30 days of receiving or creating them (Fla. Stat. 718.111(12)(g)). HOAs with 100+ parcels had to post their equivalent documents behind an owner-only portal by January 1, 2025 (Fla. Stat. 720.303). Volunteer boards miss the posting clocks, and the resident-app market serves them poorly: a TownSq reviewer, a condo president, says the app gives 'no information that allows my board to manage our association effectively'. Others report that 'mailing settings were disabled... no one received mailed statements', a 2-page PDF shows only its first page, and requests cannot be edited after submission.
solution: Boards forward minutes, bids, contracts, budgets and inspection reports to a dedicated inbox, or drop meeting recordings into a folder. The system sorts each item into the statute's document categories and redacts protected information for board approval. It posts to an owner-only portal inside the 30-day clock and keeps meeting notices and agendas on their required schedule. It expires minutes and videos on a rolling 12-month cycle and keeps a compliance scorecard showing what is posted, what is missing and when each item is due. It also logs owner records requests with response deadlines.
why_now: The posting duties are in force: the HOA portal deadline was January 1, 2025, and the condo website provision is in the current statute. Florida has also been changing its condo and HOA rules, and attorneys are warning boards about compliance. A board that receives a records demand or a lawyer's letter will pay for a fix that week. The resident apps boards would otherwise use are rated poorly for board tasks.
revenue_model: $149-$299 per month per association depending on units, plus a $500 setup fee to load and classify the existing records. Referral fees to community-association attorneys and CPAs who recommend it. Add-ons: meeting-video hosting and a document translation for multilingual communities.
non_obvious_insight: The mandate creates a legal need in the segment with the least budget. Big vendors serve professionally managed communities, while the volunteer boards of small associations only need the documents posted correctly and on time. The statute itself says a failure to post 'is not in and of itself sufficient to invalidate any action or decision' of the board and specifies no fine, so the buyer is motivated by attorney advice, owner complaints and records-request risk, not by fines or features, and the pitch should reflect that. Evidence: the statute text at http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0700-0799/0718/Sections/0718.111.html (condos) and http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0700-0799/0720/Sections/0720.303.html (HOAs, Jan 1, 2025). Resident-app gaps from TownSq Community reviews (a condo president says it provides 'no information that allows my board to manage'; disabled mailed statements; a 2-page PDF shows only page 1) at https://itunes.apple.com/us/rss/customerreviews/id=945419466/sortby=mostrecent/xml. The pain is in board and owner communication, not the payments those apps focus on.
first_30_days: Days 1-10: build the inbox-to-portal flow for the 15 statutory document types and a redaction review screen. Have a Florida community-association attorney review the category list and the redaction rules. Days 10-20: run a free public compliance scan on 200 associations in Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade using their public websites and email the board the gaps. Days 20-30: sign 2-3 community-association law firms as referral partners and take the first 10 associations at $199/month.

title: Delay-Suit Rails for Stuck Immigration Cases
one_liner: White-label filing infrastructure that lets solo immigration lawyers file mandamus/APA delay lawsuits in 48 hours, turning the government's habit of mooting suits into a flat-fee product.
customer: Solo and small immigration firms (1-10 attorneys) who pay a per-filing platform fee; end clients (naturalization, green card and employment petition applicants) pay the firm a flat $2.5-5k. Secondary buyer: employers with stuck petitions.
problem: Cases are stuck well past posted processing times: interviewed N-400s never scheduled for oath, I-485s and I-140s idling, and holds or pauses applied to nationals of dozens of countries since late 2025. Clients wait 12-30 months. Lawyers know a federal delay suit often shakes a case loose, but most solos have never filed one. Drafting the complaint, civil cover sheet, summons, service on the U.S. Attorney's civil process clerk, the Attorney General and the agency, and district-specific local rules is a 6-10 hour learning curve, and no one wants to be the first to file.
solution: A web tool with three parts. (1) An eligibility screen: enter the receipt date, form type and field office, and it compares them to posted times and to real observed outcomes, then scores the delay claim. (2) A complaint and exhibit generator with a per-district rules library, a service-of-process checklist and deadline calendar (the 60-day government answer window), and a template for the joint status report or stipulated dismissal that follows adjudication. (3) A docket-outcome database that logs, by district, judge and case type, how long from filing to adjudication. The attorney of record signs every filing. The platform is software, not a law firm.
why_now: Through late 2025 and 2026 USCIS added enhanced vetting, holds and pauses on benefit requests tied to nationality, expanded re-review of approved cases, and slower naturalization and green card scheduling. The volume of genuinely stuck cases is at a decade high. Federal courts are also less deferential to agencies since the Loper Bright decision, and adjudicating a stuck case is cheaper for the government than defending it. Solos are overloaded and short of billable-hour alternatives, so a ready-made product for a high-ticket service is easy to sell.
revenue_model: $350-600 per filing charged to the law firm (flat, not a percentage, to avoid fee-splitting rules), or $299/month for up to 3 filings. Later: a paid intelligence tier of docket-outcome analytics by district, and a litigation-funding partnership for clients who can't front the fee.
non_obvious_insight: The lawsuit is rarely litigated to judgment. The U.S. Attorney's Office usually tells USCIS to adjudicate within 30-90 days so the suit can be dismissed as moot, so the client's real purchase is a forced deadline. Clients almost never hear about this because form-prep firms earn on the application, not on pressure. Posted processing times are also misleading (they reflect only completed cases at a percentile), so whoever accumulates real time-to-decision data by field office and district owns the moat.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 immigration attorneys in high-volume districts (N.D. Cal., S.D. Tex., D.N.J., E.D.N.Y., S.D. Fla.) and offer free templates for the first filing. Build the intake screen and three complaint templates first (delayed N-400 after interview, delayed I-485, delayed I-130/I-140 or a nationality hold). Concierge-run 10 filings by hand, charging the firms $400 each. Log every outcome date, since that dataset is the product. Post outcome stats to immigration-lawyer Facebook groups and AILA chapter listservs to pull in the next 30 firms.

title: AV-TEST for Deepfake and Liveness Detectors
one_liner: A buyer-funded independent lab that red-teams deepfake and liveness detectors every month against fresh in-the-wild fakes and publishes procurement-grade scorecards.
customer: Bank and insurer model-risk and fraud-procurement teams, enterprise CISOs buying detection, media organizations, and expert witnesses. All buy annual subscriptions.
problem: Enterprise detection and IDV are the most crowded categories in the brief, and every vendor claims 95-99% accuracy on its own test set. Buyers cannot compare products. Accuracy decays with each new generator, and injection attacks bypass isolated liveness checks. Model-risk officers must validate vendor models but have no independent evidence.
solution: Maintain a continuously refreshed attack corpus: newly released generators, voice clones degraded through phone codecs, virtual-camera and emulator injection, and re-compressed video. Test vendors black-box via API and publish false-accept rates at fixed false-reject rates, cross-generator drift, and time-to-fail after each new model release. Add model-risk documentation packs and court-ready error-rate statements. Vendors may pay only for private testing, never for ranking.
why_now: Detection vendors multiplied in 2025-26 and funding is still flowing (Modulate raised $25M). The injection-attack standard CEN/TS 18099 exists but has almost no commercial third-party lab. The EU AI Act transparency deadline on 2 Dec 2026 and rising fraud losses push buyers to demand proof.
revenue_model: $15-60K per year for full scorecards and monthly refreshes. Custom bake-offs for $25-100K. Expert-witness and litigation support as an upsell.
non_obvious_insight: In the 1990s, antivirus claims were unverifiable until independent labs became the arbiter. Deepfake detection is worse because accuracy decays with every new generator, so buyers need continuous evidence, which is a recurring-revenue product. The real asset is the fresh, hard-to-game attack corpus, and no vendor can build it credibly for itself.
first_30_days: Publish a free baseline report on 10 public detectors using about 300 fresh fakes from the newest open and commercial generators. Send it to 30 bank model-risk leads. Sign 3-5 design-partner subscriptions at about $10K each.

title: Inherited Low-Rate Mortgage Concierge for Heirs
one_liner: A flat-fee service that helps heirs keep, assume or transfer a parent's low-rate mortgage instead of paying it off at closing, and values that rate as an estate asset so siblings can buy each other out fairly.
customer: Heirs (Gen X, aged 45-60) who inherit a home with a mortgage at 3-4% while new loans cost about 7.5%. The estate attorneys, probate realtors and bank trust officers who advise them refer clients and pay for tooling.
problem: The default estate path is to sell the house and pay off the loan, which destroys below-market financing. On a $300K balance at about 3.25% with 22 years left versus 7.5%, the rate is worth roughly $90K in present value (my calculation). Federal rules generally bar lenders from calling loans due on transfer to relatives at death, and confirmed successors have servicing rights under CFPB rules, but servicers are slow and inconsistent and heirs do not know. Siblings often cannot buy each other out at current rates, and a buyer's market with concessions on 44.7% of sales makes forced sales costlier.
solution: Within days of a death, verify loan type, rate, balance and assumability and confirm successor-in-interest status with the servicer. Bridge payments during probate, and produce a Rate Asset Report that values the rate for the estate inventory so heirs can split fairly. Structure buyouts with junior notes or partner lenders so one heir keeps or rents the house, and for sellers show where FHA or VA assumability lifts the sale price. Confirm applicability with counsel, since protections generally cover owner-occupied 1-4 unit homes.
why_now: Rates are rising again (Redfin: futures price the Fed funds rate at 5% by end-2027, and the 30-year is about 7.4-7.6%). A large share of Boomer mortgages sit below 4%, and the first wave of the transfer is arriving. Record concessions make selling into this market expensive. ROAD to Housing Act limits on institutional single-family owners push heirs to be small landlords.
revenue_model: $1,500-2,500 flat fee per estate or a share of rate-value preserved, a $499 Rate Asset Report, referral fees from buyout lenders, and $200 per month tooling subscriptions for probate attorneys.
non_obvious_insight: The great wealth transfer is counted in balance-sheet dollars, but in a 7.5% world the most valuable asset in many middle-class estates is the interest rate on the parent's mortgage, and the default estate process throws it away at closing.
first_30_days: Write servicer letter templates and an assumability checklist reviewed by an attorney. Recruit five probate attorneys and three probate realtors. Launch the $499 Rate Asset Report to estates with mortgages and track how many convert to the full service. Sign one HELOC or non-QM lender as buyout-financing partner.

title: Paid Exit Capture: Layoffs Become Agent Evals
one_liner: Pay departing employees a completion bonus to turn their tacit exception-handling know-how into the eval sets and edge-case playbooks the employer's AI agents need, before that knowledge walks out.
customer: Head of AI, COO or CHRO at 1,000-20,000-person companies running AI-justified headcount cuts in ops-heavy functions (claims, support, finance ops, procurement), plus PE operating partners doing portfolio-wide cuts.
problem: Companies cut the people who know the long tail, then find their agents fail on it. Reversals are now reported (Klarna rehiring humans in 2025, Commonwealth Bank of Australia reversing 45 cuts, CNBC's Jul 2026 'regret' headline). Exit interviews are HR theatre, and angry leavers have no reason to document anything.
solution: A 2-3 week 'capture sprint' inside the notice or severance window. A consented, paid interview agent plus a domain reviewer walks each person through their 50 hardest cases. Output is a graded eval set (inputs, gold decisions, rubrics, 'when I'd escalate') and a playbook the employer owns. Workers get a bonus scaled to eval quality (measured by held-out agent accuracy), a signed contribution credential and optionally a recall or contract-rights clause.
why_now: AI was the top-cited layoff reason in Challenger data for five straight months through Jul 2026, and enterprise agent rollouts are now bottlenecked by evals and edge cases rather than by models. Reversal stories are giving CFOs a fresh fear. Interview agents are cheap enough to run the sprints at scale.
revenue_model: $15-40k fixed fee per role-cluster capture sprint (roughly $1.5-4k per captured employee after bonuses), plus an annual eval-refresh retainer once the agent is live.
non_obvious_insight: To the employer a laid-off worker is a depreciating liability, but for the agent rollout they are the only source of ground truth on the long tail. You can only get it by paying, and paying on eval quality fixes the incentive. The data is worth far more than the severance delta.
first_30_days: Use public WARN filings to list 40 companies mid-layoff and pitch 15 HR/AI leads a free 5-person pilot at cost. Have an employment lawyer draft the consent, IP-assignment and NDA carve-out template. Deliver one eval set and show before/after agent accuracy as the case study.

title: Buy the Restaurant Alley: Used-Oil Route Roll-Up
one_liner: Consolidate small used-cooking-oil haulers into one AI-run route business, then sell every other mandated back-of-restaurant service from the same truck.
customer: Independent restaurants and small chains (who now get paid for their oil and buy add-on services), renewable diesel and SAF refiners buying traceable domestic feedstock, and retiring collector owners selling their routes.
problem: From 2026 the 45Z clean-fuel credit applies only to North American feedstock, and UCO prices have run at roughly $1,000 to $1,400 per tonne. Restaurants historically gave oil away under auto-renewing contracts with big renderers, and theft is common. Small collectors lack chain-of-custody paperwork and contamination grading, and refiners want traceable domestic supply.
solution: Acquire 8 to 15 small collectors, grease-trap pumpers and hood cleaners in one metro. AI ops: fill-level sensors or photo estimates to cut truck miles 25% to 40%, vision-based contamination grading at pickup, automatic chain-of-custody and sustainability documentation for refiners, and a contract-reading agent that finds competitors' termination windows and times win-back offers. Add hood cleaning, grease-trap pumping and fire-suppression inspection on the same route visits.
why_now: 45Z limits credits to North American feedstock from 2026, which makes domestic UCO scarce and valuable, and documentation that used to be optional is now a selling point. Owners of small routes are aging out, and route-optimization and photo-grading tools are cheap.
revenue_model: Spread on oil resale to refiners with a share paid to restaurants, plus $150 to $500 per add-on service visit, plus a traceability premium from refiners.
non_obvious_insight: The real asset isn't the trucks; it's the contract calendar. Thousands of evergreen grease agreements with 30 to 90 day cancellation windows can be read, mapped and timed. The alley visit is also the cheapest customer touchpoint for every other mandated back-of-house service.
first_30_days: Approach a retiring one-truck collector about a seller-financed purchase in the $200k to $600k range, or start as a broker with a subcontracted truck offering 20 to 30 restaurants a paid pickup. Build a photo-based intake and contract tracker. Target franchisee groups with 5 to 10 units. Pre-sell forward oil volume to a regional biodiesel or renewable diesel refiner using documented chain of custody.

title: Turn Podcast Fans Into Local Chapters
one_liner: A chapter-in-a-box that lets mid-size creators convert engaged, lonely audiences into weekly local meetups, with insurance, host training and venues handled.
customer: Superfans aged 18-34 paying about $12 a month for a local chapter. Creators with 50k-1M followers are the distribution partners on a revenue share. Brand sponsors pay for chapter access.
problem: Insiders treat parasocial attachment as a symptom of loneliness. But an audience with a shared in-group reference is already a pre-formed community, and creators' inboxes are full of 'is there a meetup in my city?' Creators cannot run 40 city chapters themselves because of liability, hosting, venues and safety. Discord and online-only communities do not fix in-person isolation.
solution: The platform reads audience data to find the top 10 fan-dense cities per creator. It recruits and trains volunteer hosts from top fans, provides liability insurance, a code of conduct and venue partnerships (breweries, cafes), and delivers a monthly 'creator drop' built for group listening or viewing. Each chapter runs weekly or biweekly with a 30-40 member target.
why_now: Fan-led IRL groups (run clubs, book clubs, hobby meetups) exploded through 2024-25. Feed fatigue and AI-slop backlash push young adults toward real-world belonging. Creators need revenue beyond volatile ad and sponsor income, and Meetup's post-acquisition policy troubles have left organizers looking for alternatives.
revenue_model: 20-25% of chapter dues, venue referral fees and sponsor packages. A 40-member chapter at $12 a month is $480 a month. Creators keep about 40% of dues.
non_obvious_insight: Parasocial is not the disease, it is the on-ramp. The cheapest cold start for local community is an audience that already shares references. What is missing is boring, outsourceable logistics and risk management.
first_30_days: Sign 3 niche-hobby creators with 100-300k audiences. Use their email or Patreon ZIP-code data to pick one city each. Recruit hosts from their Discords. Run the first brewery meetups and charge $12 a month from day one, aiming for 30 members per chapter.

title: Battery Passport Onboarding for E-Bike and Storage Makers
one_liner: Done-for-you EU battery passport, QR labelling and supplier data collection for makers of e-bikes, scooters and industrial or stationary batteries facing the 18 Feb 2027 date.
customer: Mid-size e-bike, e-scooter and light-EV brands, industrial battery pack assemblers and BESS integrators selling in the EU (20-500 staff), plus importers who count as the manufacturer.
problem: The EU Battery Regulation requires from 18 Feb 2027 a QR code and electronic battery passport for EV, light-transport and industrial batteries above 2 kWh (background knowledge; verify current status and any slippage). The data spans composition, cell supplier, recycled content, carbon footprint and state of health, and it must be extracted from cell makers who resist sharing. Larger passport vendors serve automakers and big OEMs, so small assemblers fall through.
solution: A supplier data-collection portal with templates for cell makers, a passport record generator with public and restricted access tiers, QR label files, state-of-health data hooks, a compliance checklist and change updates, plus a service layer that chases suppliers until they answer.
why_now: About 20 weeks remain, delegated acts and standards are still in flux, and small makers cannot wait for perfect specs. Even if parts slip, buyers still need the underlying data.
revenue_model: EUR 8-30k onboarding plus EUR 3-10k/year platform per battery family, with supplier-chasing billed hourly.
non_obvious_insight: The passport is a supplier-data-chasing problem, not a blockchain problem. Small buyers can pool leverage as a buying club so a cell maker answers one questionnaire instead of fifty.
first_30_days: Compile 200 EU e-bike and light-EV brands via a trade body and email a 'passport readiness scorecard'. Sign five design partners at EUR 5k and negotiate a template data sheet with two cell makers.

title: Alternative-Use Memos for Office Special Servicers
one_liner: A fixed-fee, five-day, non-conflicted resolution memo (convert, hold, sell, owner-user sale) for distressed office loans, written for the asset status report.
customer: CMBS special servicers, directing certificateholders (B-piece buyers), CRE CLO managers and bank special-assets groups handling office loans.
problem: About 15.7% of office CMBS is in special servicing, $39B matures within 12 months, and 71% of distressed balance is refinance failure rather than missed payments. Advice comes from brokers paid on transactions, and the standard resolution package (appraisal and broker opinion) rarely tests conversion, condo-ization or owner-user sale.
solution: An automated building screen (floor-plate depth, core, window line, structure, zoning, incentives, land-value floor) plus a local architect and contractor sanity check, delivered as a ranked options memo with recovery ranges, formatted for the asset status report. Public CMBS filings are used to prospect.
why_now: The 2026-2028 maturity wall is large and incentives for conversion are spreading. Vision and language models can screen buildings from public records, and servicers need defensible analysis for decisions that are now contested.
revenue_model: $6-12K per asset, sold in prepaid batches; retainers for servicers with 20+ office assets.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyer is the directing certificateholder who bears the loss and can direct disposition, and the cost is typically reimbursable from the loan and trivial against a $50M balance. A conflict-free second opinion can move recovery by points.
first_30_days: Use public CMBS filings to list 200 transferred office loans. Send a free sample memo on one publicly identifiable loan to asset managers at 10 mid-tier servicers and 5 directing holders. Price at $7.5K and target three paid pilots.

title: Provenance Stamps for AI-Drafted Official Products
one_liner: A document layer that makes AI-assisted analytic and official products visibly claim-by-claim traceable, and refuses to export as official until unsupported claims are resolved.
customer: State and regional fusion centers, police intelligence units, commercial OSINT and threat-intel shops selling to government, and city attorneys' offices. DoD follows later via integrators.
problem: A SOCOM analyst's chatbot invented a ship's cargo manifest, and it was formatted into an official-looking intelligence summary before aircraft were airborne. Insiders say better models will fix hallucination. The real failure is laundered credibility: AI-formatted output looks signed and trusted.
solution: A Word and Docs add-in that tags every sentence as source-linked, analyst-asserted or model-generated. Model-generated claims carry a visible marker. Official templates and PDF export are blocked until each claim has a source or a named human sign-off. It produces a hashed provenance record for later review.
why_now: GenAI.mil hit more than 2M users in one week, and 100k custom agents exist. The SOCOM story is public, and government AI-governance guidance is hardening. Buyers can now cite a concrete incident.
revenue_model: $40-90 per user per month, with agency site licenses of $50-250K. Enterprise add-ons for audit reporting.
non_obvious_insight: The fix is friction, not accuracy. Sell a product that deliberately makes AI-drafted content look unofficial until a human has vouched for it, so trust cannot be laundered through formatting.
first_30_days: Ship the add-in for one document type, such as a threat bulletin. Recruit 3 fusion centers and 2 OSINT vendors as design partners. Build a demo that replays the SOCOM failure and shows it being blocked.

title: Cooler-Door Pivot for THC Beverage Brands
one_liner: A 45-day pivot studio that moves hemp-THC drink and gummy brands into compliant functional products under their existing distributor and retailer slots, plus a per-container THC ledger for distributors and retailers.
customer: Small and mid-size hemp-THC beverage and edible brands, beverage distributors including alcohol-licensed ones, and convenience, liquor and smoke-shop chains holding hemp SKUs. Brands pay for the pivot sprint and co-pack. Distributors and retailers pay a subscription for the SKU ledger.
problem: P.L. 119-37 redefines hemp to 0.4 mg total THC per container. The effective date was pushed from Nov 12 to Dec 11, 2026 by H.R. 6500 (signed Sept 2), while synthetic cannabinoids lose hemp status on Nov 12. The US Hemp Roundtable estimates about 95% of existing products fall outside the new definition, and a typical THC drink has 2-10 mg per can. There is no federal sell-through safe harbor. The industry employs about 350,000 people. Distributors are asking whether alcohol-licensed wholesalers can even accept returns in three-tier states, and operators face a liquidity problem, not a compliance problem.
solution: Two parts. First, an SKU ledger where COAs and pack volumes are converted into per-container total THC (delta-9 plus decarboxylated THCA) and a keep, pull or return status by state, with vendor chargeback letters and a documented disposition trail. Second, a pivot studio that reuses the brand's flavor systems, cans and design to launch adaptogen, functional or non-alcoholic SKUs through a vetted co-packer, so the brand keeps its distributor agreements and planogram slots. An optional bridge licenses the brand to a state-licensed cannabis producer, since licensed dispensaries are unaffected by the federal redefinition.
why_now: The reprieve to Dec 11 gives roughly 10 weeks. Four congressional frameworks are pending: Barr, Van Duyne and Landsman, Comer, and a Sheehy-Klobuchar Senate companion. The ledger works whether Congress bans or regulates, because age-21, testing and labeling regimes would still need lab-verified per-container data. Retailers and distributors are already telling counsel to audit inventory and plan wind-downs, and gummy prices are reported at 30-50% of 2025 levels.
revenue_model: $5-15k fixed fee per brand pivot sprint, plus a 2-5% royalty or co-pack margin on the pivot SKUs. $199-499 per month per distributor or retail chain for the SKU ledger and chargeback tooling. Finder fee on brand-licensing deals to licensed operators.
non_obvious_insight: As Harris Sliwoski puts it, 'The problem for many operators will not be compliance but liquidity' (https://harris-sliwoski.com/cannalawblog/what-the-2026-federal-hemp-ban-means-for-unsold-hemp-inventory/). The scarce asset of a THC-drink brand is not inventory, which is illiquid and repricing downward, but its cooler-door slots and distributor agreements, which are among the hardest things to win in beverages. Those slots vanish if the brand disappears. The per-container standard turns an impossible reformulation into a category switch: LearnBrands notes the demand is being inherited by non-alcoholic beer, alcohol-removed wine and functional beverages (https://www.learnbrands.com/post/hemp-thc-beverage-ban-november-2026). Sources on the reprieve and stakes: https://foleyhoag.com/news-and-insights/blogs/cannabis-and-the-law/2026/september/a-temporary-reprieve-for-hemp-thc-products%E2%80%A6-but-what-now/ and https://www.ediblerank.com/legal/hemp-ban-timeline
first_30_days: Pull 40 THC-beverage brands from distributor and retailer press lists and offer a free exposure scan built from their COAs and volumes. Sell three paid pivot sprints. Line up one co-packer with non-alcoholic and adaptogen capability. Pilot the SKU ledger with two distributors and one c-store chain, producing their pull and return list.

title: Data Act Unlock for Hotel Connected Equipment
one_liner: Use the EU Data Act's user-access rights to pull hotels' own data out of locked vendor clouds (HVAC, locks, laundry, elevators) into an energy and maintenance ledger that third-party service firms can plug into.
customer: EU independent hotel groups and management companies with 5-50 properties, plus independent HVAC, elevator and kitchen-equipment service firms and energy-optimization vendors that want the data.
problem: After the 2026 Hormuz energy shock, hotel energy costs have been repriced sharply. The data from a hotel's connected thermostats, HVAC, locks, laundry and elevators is trapped in manufacturers' clouds, resold as premium dashboards or API fees. A mixed-brand group cannot build a unified view, and independent maintenance firms cannot diagnose without OEM tools.
solution: Since Sep 2025 the Data Act has let users demand the data generated by connected products and have it shared with a third party they choose (free to the user, on my reading, so verify). New products must offer access by design from 12 Sep 2026. The service is a request desk (letter templates, deadline tracking per OEM, escalation to the national authority) plus connectors that load the data into a property energy and asset ledger, with consent logs for designated recipients.
why_now: The Sep 2026 design-by-default date has just passed and vendors are unprepared, so early requests set the precedents. Energy-cost pain makes the hotel side motivated. The brief also shows small hardware makers scrambling with Data Act and CRA duties, so vendors are stretched.
revenue_model: About EUR 200 per property per month, 10-15% of verified energy savings, and onboarding fees paid by service firms and optimizers who become designated recipients.
non_obvious_insight: Hotels are among the largest accidental 'users' under the Data Act, with dozens of connected products per building, and nobody has told them. The law turns vendor lock-in into a right, the way GDPR created a market for data-subject-request services.
first_30_days: Sign one 10-property group for a flat EUR 1,500 'Data Act audit plus first requests'. Inventory its connected assets, send about 20 access requests across 5 OEMs, and document responses and escalations. Then sell the same audit to 4 more groups and pitch one independent service firm as a designated recipient.

title: PFAS Land-Application History Reports for Farmland
one_liner: A 'Phase I environmental site assessment' for PFAS on farmland, built from biosolids land-application records and upstream discharger data, sold to lenders, farmland funds and appraisers before the sensors exist.
customer: Farm Credit associations and ag banks, farmland investment funds, rural appraisers and title firms, and farmers or buyers who need to show a field is clean.
problem: EPA released Draft Guidance for Reducing Risk from PFOA and PFOS in Biosolids on July 1, 2026, noting that sewage sludge may carry PFAS from industrial dischargers, landfills and homes. Yet EPA's own FY2026 SBIR Phase I topics still ask small businesses to invent 'Treatment of PFAS in Wastewater Sewage Sludge and Biosolids' and 'Sensors to Detect PFAS in Environmental Matrices', so cheap field screening does not exist. Lenders and buyers are pricing farmland today with no way to know whether a field received sludge, from which plant, and with what upstream industrial inputs.
solution: A desktop screening report per parcel. It combines state biosolids land-application permits and site reports (obtained by scraping and automated public-records requests), the treatment plant's upstream industrial dischargers, soil and hydrology data, and a risk tier. Higher tiers trigger a sampling plan run by a partner lab using EPA Method 1633. Deliver in the lender's existing environmental-diligence workflow, and later offer an API.
why_now: The July 1, 2026 EPA draft guidance turns PFAS in biosolids from a research topic into something lenders must ask about. EPA's Sept 24, 2026 SBIR solicitation ($100k per Phase I, 6 months, closes Nov 8, 2026) is paying for the sensing tools, so cheap field tests are years away and records-based screening is the only option now.
revenue_model: $400 to $1,200 per desktop parcel report. $2k to $6k with coordinated sampling (margin on lab work). $20k to $60k per year API or portfolio subscriptions for lenders and farmland funds.
non_obvious_insight: The government is paying to invent PFAS sensors that don't exist yet, but the lend/buy/insure decision is being made now on paper records, so the winning product is the record-linkage layer, not the sensor. EPA's FY2026 SBIR Phase I topics list 1B (PFAS in sewage sludge and biosolids) and 2A (PFAS sensors in environmental matrices), $100,000 and 6 months each: https://www.epa.gov/sbir/how-apply-sbir-contract. EPA's biosolids page lists the July 1, 2026 Draft Guidance and states that sludge may carry PFAS from upstream dischargers: https://www.epa.gov/biosolids. Lenders already require site assessments for gas stations and dry cleaners, and a PFAS-on-farmland version is the missing sibling. Caveat: the EPA pages I could fetch gave no land-application tonnage or state-by-state record availability, so records access must be checked before committing to a state.
first_30_days: Pick 1 or 2 states where biosolids land-application permits are public (verify first). Assemble records for the 20 largest treatment plants and build 25 sample reports on real parcels. Approach 5 Farm Credit associations, 3 farmland funds and 5 rural appraisers with a free report on a parcel they already own or are underwriting. Sign a lab partner for sampling. Close the first 3 paid pilots at $400 to $1,200 per parcel.

title: Teleoperated Pack-and-Pick Robots Piloted from Latin America
one_liner: Robot arms run by foundation models, with remote pilots in Guatemala or Colombia fixing the edge cases, sold per box.
customer: Berry, tomato and cucumber packhouses and greenhouses that lost crews.
problem: Farm labor shrank by at least 155,000 and crews were lost in 2026 harvests, while robots pick at 50-60% of human speed and fail on edge cases.
solution: Rent arms with a vision-language-action stack for clamshell packing, and route failures to remote operators at roughly one pilot per 8-10 arms, priced per case.
why_now: Physical-AI models matured in 2025-26, remote-assist tooling and satellite or 5G links are cheap, and enforcement removed the informal labor pool.
revenue_model: Per-case fee with a minimum monthly commitment per station.
non_obvious_insight: Robots run about 20 hours a day at half human speed, and remote humans fix the rare failures. The result is a labor channel that needs neither a visa nor a robot that never fails.
first_30_days: Rent two arms, set up a clamshell-packing station at one packhouse, and hire three remote operators for a paid pilot.

title: Front Door for AI Callers at Local Businesses
one_liner: A phone-number layer that recognizes when the caller is an AI agent, answers instantly with pre-authorized quotes and availability, and routes real customers to humans.
customer: Owner-operated local service businesses (salons, groomers, HVAC and plumbing, auto shops, cleaners) with 1-20 staff, reached via marketing agencies and booking or field-service platforms. AI receptionist vendors are later licensees.
problem: Google's 'Have AI check pricing' agentic calling has rolled out to US Search users and expanded to home services in summer 2026. Businesses now get AI callers that tie up staff and harvest prices, and owners cannot tell agents from customers. In Microsoft's Magentic Marketplace simulation, buyer agents heavily favored the first proposal they received, so fast structured answers win business.
solution: Answer with an agent detector and an agent lane. If the caller identifies as or behaves like an AI (or presents a signed handshake), reply with a spoken and machine-readable quote from the owner's rate card and calendar within owner-set bounds, and log the outcome. Real customers go to humans. Publish a URL or DTMF handshake so compliant agents can switch from speech to structured data, the Gibberlink idea done with production-grade channels. Analytics show which agents call and quote win rates.
why_now: Agentic calling is live at Google scale, AI receptionists are common, and the 2025 Gibberlink demo proved the handshake idea but remains a proof of concept. Production agent protocols (MCP, A2A) do not cover phone calls to small businesses.
revenue_model: $49-$149/month per location, agency white-label deals, and later per-verified-handshake fees from agent platforms.
non_obvious_insight: The phone is the API of the local economy and both ends are becoming machines that still talk in speech. Whoever owns the switch-to-data handshake and the seller's rate-card truth owns local agent commerce, and speed to first quote may matter more than price.
first_30_days: Build the call flow on a telephony API. Recruit 20 salons, groomers and HVAC shops through 3 local marketing agencies, log the AI calls they receive (many owners are unaware), and show AI calls answered and quotes won. Charge $79/month.

title: Finish Crew: Stranded Solar Job Completion
one_liner: A completion contractor that takes half-built solar jobs abandoned by bankrupt installers all the way to permission-to-operate, and is paid by the lenders whose loans go bad while the system sits dark.
customer: Solar loan originators and servicers, and TPO sponsors, that now hold stranded projects. The seven finance partners named in the Freedom Forever order are the first buyers: GoodLeap, EnFin, Credit Human, EverBright, Participate, Project Solar and Sunrun. Credit unions and ABS trustees holding 2023-2025 solar loans are the second wave. Homeowners are the beneficiary but do not pay.
problem: When a big installer dies, thousands of systems are left installed but not energized, or half-built. Freedom Forever went Chapter 11 in April 2026 and converted to Chapter 7 on Aug 7, 2026, with about 1,600 layoffs. The borrower stops paying a $30-50k loan on a roof that produces nothing. Lender, homeowner and dead installer each say it is someone else's job. The court let lenders hire new contractors and push systems to PTO, but a lender has no bench of crews and no playbook for doing it.
solution: Run the work as a records-recovery business first and a crew business second. For each stranded job, build a forensic pack: the AHJ permit file, the utility interconnection record, the design set from the dead company's design and CRM tools, equipment serials from distributors and consignment records, and a site photo audit. Sort jobs into tiers: paperwork-only (contractor of record and engineer's stamp need re-issuing), inspection fix, missing hardware, and never started (unwind and refund path). Price each tier at a fixed fee plus a bonus at PTO, and subcontract the labor to licensed local electricians and laid-off installer crews. Give the lender a dashboard of its whole stranded book with cost to cure and expected PTO date.
why_now: Freedom Forever's Chapter 7 conversion (Aug 2026, creditor claims due Oct 16, 2026) and the court order letting financiers step in make this concrete now. Sunnova (June 2025), SunPower (Aug 2024) and 100+ other solar failures came before it. Post-25D volume is down in 2026, so more failures are likely. Lenders have step-in rights but no operating capacity.
revenue_model: Fixed completion fee of $1.5-4k per job by tier, plus a $500 success bonus at PTO, paid by the lender or servicer. Add a monthly stranded-book dashboard subscription. Later, sell a 12-month workmanship warranty on completed jobs, paid by the lender, and a retainer for standby capacity when the next installer fails.
non_obvious_insight: A stranded job is 80% a records and legal-standing problem, not a labor problem. Permits, interconnection applications, engineer stamps and design files sit in a dead contractor's name and portal logins, so nobody can legally finish even though laid-off crews are cheap and plentiful. Also, the buyer is the lender and not the homeowner. The lender's collateral is worthless while the system is dark, it already has contractual step-in rights, and outsiders assume the homeowner is the customer.
first_30_days: Message loss-mitigation and installer-failure leads at 3-4 lenders. Use former installer ops people on LinkedIn to get the introductions. Offer to complete 10 stranded jobs in one metro at cost-plus, with payment on PTO. Recruit 3 laid-off project managers or permit coordinators and 1-2 licensed electrician subs. Write the per-AHJ and per-utility contractor-of-record transfer checklist. Target the first 10 PTOs inside 60 days, with case studies from them.

title: Farm-to-Factory Water Supply Assurance
one_liner: A diligence-plus-settlement service that sells expanding plants a permit-grade, verified acre-foot supply by leasing fallowed farm water in drought-stressed Western basins.
customer: Plant developers, site-selection teams and economic-development agencies for semiconductor, pharma and food plants in AZ, TX, ID and UT. Irrigation districts and farmers are the supply side.
problem: Water is now a siting gate: Texas froze grid connections over water, the Colorado River's 2027-2036 framework forces farm cuts, and Amazon put $20M into farm conservation with no settlement layer. Factories need a legally defensible supply and 'water neutral' commitments, and farmers cannot easily sell verified savings.
solution: Start with a $15-40k water-supply diligence report (rights, drought exposure, discharge capacity, PFAS in source). Then structure and meter option-style leases with farmers, with satellite and meter verification, and issue an assurance letter usable in permitting.
why_now: The Aug 2026 Colorado River Record of Decision, 49.6% of the US in drought, and reshoring in water-intensive sectors (electronics +35%, pharma +32%, food +17% in robot orders) collide.
revenue_model: Diligence fee plus 5-8% of lease flow and a verification fee per acre-foot.
non_obvious_insight: The cheapest new industrial water supply is a farmer's fallowed field, but only if someone provides the paperwork that turns it into a permit-grade asset.
first_30_days: Pick one county (for example Pinal, AZ). Sign three farmers on non-binding option terms. Sell two diligence reports to plant real-estate teams or EDCs, and recruit a water-rights attorney as an advisor.

title: Royalty Co-op for Expert Robot Demonstrations
one_liner: A worker-owned data cooperative where master tradespeople record their skilled work and earn ongoing royalties when robot makers license the demonstrations.
customer: Payers are robot foundation-model teams and manipulation or humanoid startups that buy data. Suppliers are skilled tradespeople such as tire techs, electricians, welders and HVAC technicians.
problem: Data platforms pay flat hourly rates for average people making coffee. Robots need expert-quality demonstrations, and experts will not sell their edge for a one-time $20 an hour or train their own replacement without control and upside.
solution: Partner with a union local or trade school. Members use standardized capture kits (head and wrist cameras, gloves) with quality scoring. They get a guaranteed hourly rate, 30-50% of licensing revenue, and a veto over use cases. Buyers pay per curated dataset plus a royalty per training run.
why_now: Robot training data is the humanoid bottleneck. XDOF reached about $50M annualized revenue within three months of stealth, and Mecka projects $100M ARR by end-2026 on a roughly $500M valuation. Willingness to pay is proven, while worker anxiety about being trained out of a job is rising.
revenue_model: $50-500k per dataset license, with a 20-30% cooperative fee on royalties and licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Data quality follows expert willingness, and willingness follows ownership. A cooperative with collective pricing power is a supply moat that flat-wage crowd platforms cannot copy, and it turns worker fear into the product's selling point.
first_30_days: Partner with one trade school and one union local in tire and auto service or EV-charger installation. Recruit 20 masters and capture 200 hours of one task family. Sell a pilot dataset to 2 robotics startups at $30-80k.

title: Burn-Lot Exit Desk for Fire Survivors
one_liner: Package burned lots and stranded insurance claims into sellable assets, and auction them to vetted builders at fair prices.
customer: Owners of destroyed lots in the Palisades and Altadena (free to them). Builders, small developers and community land trusts pay a success fee.
problem: About 13% of affected Palisades single-family owners have started rebuilding 18-plus months on. Insurer estimates ($462/sq ft) sit far below contractor budgets (up to $1,065). Many owners do not want to become developers, and cash buyers lowball lots.
solution: Prepare each lot as a marketable asset: claim documents (what transfers and what does not), debris and utility status, pre-approved plans and permit history. Run a competitive bid among vetted builders with three options: sell the lot, sell with claim assignment, or take a fixed-price turnkey rebuild. Handle escrow and title through partners.
why_now: Deadlines on additional-living-expense coverage and permit pipelines are biting 18 months after the fires, and the low rebuild rate shows demand for an exit.
revenue_model: A 2-3% buyer-paid success fee, builder subscriptions for deal flow, and later turnkey rebuild margin.
non_obvious_insight: 'Rebuilding services' is the obvious market. The larger one is liquidity: turning a lot plus a claim into cash at a fair price.
first_30_days: Interview 30 owners in fire-survivor groups, recruit 3 builders, and hand-run 5 lots. Use a licensed broker partner for the transaction side.

title: Make Platforms and Receiving Banks Pay Scam Refunds
one_liner: A contingency-fee desk that packages evidence so banks can recover mandatory scam reimbursements from receiving institutions and, in the EU, from the platforms where the scam ran.
customer: UK and EU challenger banks, building societies, credit unions, and e-money and payment institutions. Buyers are fraud-recovery and operations heads.
problem: In the UK, PSPs have had to reimburse authorized push-payment scam victims up to GBP 85K since Oct 2024, with the cost split 50:50 between sending and receiving firms. The EU's provisional PSR deal extends liability to bank-impersonation scams and to platforms that ignore fraud notices. Banks treat reimbursement as a cost of business. Recovering from the other side of the chain (the mule-hosting bank, the ad or profile platform) is manual, slow, and mostly abandoned.
solution: Ingest reimbursed case files and auto-build claim dossiers: a timeline, hash-stamped screenshots of the scam ad or profile, the platform notification and its response time, mule-account indicators, and a funds trace. File claims through scheme channels and formal notices to platforms. Track deadlines and disputes. Get paid a percentage of what is actually recovered.
why_now: Mandatory reimbursement now has more than a year of claim volume in the UK. The EU deal shifts costs toward platforms. Investigations into scam-ad revenue have made platform accountability a political priority. Nobody yet holds the data on which counterparties pay and how fast.
revenue_model: 15-25% contingency on recovered value, with a small SaaS floor. A mid-size UK institution reimbursing GBP 10-30M a year can justify six-figure annual fees.
non_obvious_insight: Liability rules create a claims market. The value chain of counterparties is unbilled because banks were told to reimburse victims, not to chase others, and the recovery data is a compounding moat. Whoever holds it can also sell it to regulators.
first_30_days: Offer 10 UK EMIs and small banks a free audit of 50 reimbursed cases showing recoverable amounts from receiving-side firms and disputed shares. Sign contingency contracts with the first 3. Hire one ex-fraud-ops analyst and use spreadsheets and templates before automating.

title: Clinic-Sponsored Tuition for Loan-Capped PT Students
one_liner: Sports-medicine PT and athletic-training employers fund tuition for students shut out of federal loans, in return for a structured work commitment.
customer: Multi-site outpatient orthopedic and sports PT groups, performance-rehab clinics and athletic-training staffing contractors pay the fee. The beneficiaries are DPT and athletic-training students facing the new loan caps.
problem: Since July 1, 2026, grad loans are capped at $20.5k a year and $100k total, and PT, OT, nursing and counseling were left out of the 'professional' tier ($50k a year, $200k total). A $100-150k DPT can no longer be financed federally. Private lenders are tightening, some loans reach 16% APR, and disbursements ran up to 6 weeks late. Meanwhile clinics have chronic PT vacancies and pay recruiters roughly 15-25% of first-year salary per hire.
solution: A sponsored-seat platform. The clinic pledges tuition support paid directly to the school, using tax-free employer educational assistance (up to $5,250 a year under Section 127) plus scholarship funds. The student signs a transparent 3-year post-licensure commitment with pro-rated forgiveness, structured around state limits on stay-or-pay clauses. We handle matching, contracts, compliance and servicing. Any remaining gap routes to a CDFI or credit-union partner that underwrites on the employer's offer.
why_now: The caps went live with the fall 2026 semester, so the first affected cohorts are hitting the gap now. A healthcare-association lawsuit (suspension deadline December 2026) adds uncertainty, so students and programs want a hedge whichever way it goes. Recruiting costs are high, and the tax-free employer student-loan-repayment exclusion was made permanent in 2025.
revenue_model: A success fee of 8-12% of first-year salary (about $9-13k per seat), below the recruiter benchmark: one third at contract signing, the rest at licensure start. Plus a servicing fee of 0.5-1% on managed balances and a referral fee from the partner lender.
non_obvious_insight: Federal caps have made employers the only underwriter that can price DPT risk, because salary, licensure pass rates and vacancy cost are all known. For a clinic group, tuition-for-service is a cheaper and stickier recruiting channel than a 20% recruiter fee. It also locks in local talent in the years when the pipeline shrinks.
first_30_days: Recruit 8-10 PT-group owners through APTA state chapters and practice-owner communities. Sign 10 sponsored seats for the Jan/Aug 2027 cohorts. Ask 3-4 DPT programs' financial-aid offices to introduce enrolled students with funding gaps. Use a counsel-drafted contract template. No lending is needed at first; the launch product is a paid placement plus a contract.
